summary: App needs an industry-standard IPFS/Pinata NFT upload workflow: lock assets, upload images folder to get IMAGES_FOLDER_CID, inject image URIs into per-token metadata JSON files, then upload metadata folder to get METADATA_FOLDER_CID (for marketplace tokenURIs), without changing existing features or UI layout.
architectural_notes: Pinata uploads must use directory paths in multipart FormData (3rd arg filename like "metadata/1.json") so Pinata creates folders rather than collapsing/merging into a single file.
Workflow requires two separate Pinata uploads: images folder first to obtain IMAGES_FOLDER_CID, then metadata folder after rewriting image URIs to ipfs://IMAGES_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.png.
known_issues: Metadata upload to Pinata is currently being merged into a single file (e.g., MONKE_INDEX_metadata.json) instead of a metadata folder containing per-token JSON files.

existing_features.title: Update the IPFS/Pinata upload workflow to exactly follow: (1) upload the entire images folder as a single directory upload and receive IMAGES_FOLDER_CID; (2) generate one metadata JSON file per token with an `image` field set to `ipfs://IMAGES_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.png`; (3) upload the entire metadata folder as a single directory upload and receive METADATA_FOLDER_CID; and (4) present the final token URI format as `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json`.

Fix Pinata directory upload construction so directory uploads cannot collapse/merge metadata into a single file: ensure every file appended to `FormData` for directory uploads includes the intended per-file path/name (via the third parameter of `formData.append('file', blob, <path>)`) and that metadata is uploaded as multiple files (`1.json`, `2.json`, …) inside one directory upload.

Enforce 1-based sequential filenames for both exported assets and Pinata uploads: images must be named `1.png`, `2.png`, `3.png`, … and metadata files must be `1.json`, `2.json`, `3.json`, … (no `0.png`/`0.json` in the IPFS upload workflow).

Implement final asset locking behavior: when the collection is locked for publishing, disable the Vault "Generate" action (and any regeneration actions that would change the collection) and only re-enable them after the collection is unlocked, without changing the current app layout.

Ensure exported images match the exact pixel dimensions configured in the Settings section for the project, and that the same sizing is used for the images that are uploaded to Pinata (so all assets in the uploaded images folder share identical dimensions).

Keep the existing upload controls flow (Lock → Upload → Unlock) but update status/output text to clearly show both returned CIDs (IMAGES_FOLDER_CID and METADATA_FOLDER_CID) and the final token URI format `ipfs://METADATA_FOLDER_CID/<TOKEN_ID>.json`, using English for all user-facing text.

new_feature_requests.summary: Implement industry-standard IPFS/Pinata workflow: lock assets, disable Generate while locked, enforce sequential filenames, upload images folder -> IMAGES_FOLDER_CID, inject image URIs into per-token metadata JSON, upload metadata folder -> METADATA_FOLDER_CID
Fix Pinata metadata upload so metadata is uploaded as a folder of individual JSON files (e.g., 1.json, 2.json, ...) instead of being merged into a single aggregated metadata file

Add one-click end-to-end Upload action that automatically performs images upload, metadata rewriting with IMAGES_FOLDER_CID, then metadata folder upload, producing final marketplace-ready tokenURI base (METADATA_FOLDER_CID)
Support 1-based token naming/numbering for assets and metadata (1.png/1.json, 2.png/2.json, ...) to match the required workflow and marketplaces expectations

projectName: Implement industry-standard Pinata directory upload workflow (images CID + per-token metadata CID) with asset locking
